cases.question: Why can LoRA avoid adding inference latency once a task-specific adapter has been trained?

provenance.license: Source paper terms apply; distributed by arXiv.

annotation.notes: Source-audited on 2026-08-30 against checksum-pinned LoRA v2 page 4; the automated judge remains advisory.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

expected.reference_answer: At deployment, LoRA can explicitly form and store W = W0 + BA and then run inference as usual. Because the low-rank update is merged into the base weight instead of evaluated as a separate serial module, it does not add inference latency.

answer_criteria.description: States that W0 and BA can be merged into W = W0 + BA.
States that inference then proceeds as usual without a separate adapter path.
Connects the merge to no additional inference latency.

forbidden_claims: Claims LoRA eliminates all model inference time or reports a numerical latency speedup.

gold_evidence.section: 4.1 Low-Rank-Parametrized Update Matrices / No Additional Inference Latency
gold_evidence.quote: We can explicitly compute and store W = W0 + BA and perform inference as usual. Note that both W0 and BA are in R^(d x k). When we need to switch to another downstream task, we can recover W0 by subtracting BA and then adding a different B'A', a quick operation with very little memory overhead. Critically, this guarantees that we do not introduce any additional latency during inference compared to a fine-tuned model by construction.

cases.question: How is a LoRA weight update parameterized as a low-rank decomposition, and which quantities are trainable?

provenance.license: Source paper terms apply; distributed by arXiv.
provenance.adaptation_notes: Question and rubric authored from the checksum-pinned v2 full text.

annotation.notes: Source-audited on 2026-08-30 against checksum-pinned LoRA v2 page 4, including the full equation and definitions; the automated judge remains advisory.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

expected.reference_answer: For a pretrained weight W0, LoRA constrains the update as Delta W = BA, so the forward pass uses W0 + BA. W0 remains frozen while A and B are trainable, with rank r much smaller than the original matrix dimensions.

answer_criteria.description: States that the update is parameterized as Delta W = BA and the effective weight is W0 + BA.
States that W0 is frozen.
States that A and B are trainable.
States that r is much smaller than the original dimensions.

forbidden_claims: Claims W0, A, and B are all trained together.

gold_evidence.quote: For a pre-trained weight matrix W0 in R^(d x k), we constrain its update by representing the latter with a low-rank decomposition W0 + Delta W = W0 + BA, where B in R^(d x r), A in R^(r x k), and the rank r << min(d, k). During training, W0 is frozen and does not receive gradient updates, while A and B contain trainable parameters.

Claims RAG represents task adaptation only as low-rank weight updates.

gold_evidence.quote: We propose Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, which freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture, greatly reducing the number of trainable parameters for downstream tasks.
We introduce RAG models where the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever.

challenge.description: The evaluator must preserve which adaptation mechanism belongs to each paper and cover both required revisions.
